description: Static diagnostic chosen after reading the bank. Score check-action words +2 and shortcut words -3; average tied maxima equally. This is not a blind learner trial, browser score, or validated item-difficulty measure.
positive: check inspect correct resolve remove verify review recalculate regenerate reconcile trace measure
negative: only trust assume ignore immediately without regardless guarantees

rows.prompt: The two AA cells are still in the holder while you change a wire. What should you do before moving it?
You want to know whether a jumper wire connects to an LED lead on a breadboard. The cells are removed. Which tool and setting would help?
Your unpowered check finds continuity directly between the holder’s positive and negative terminals with the switch closed. What is the next step?
The switch is closed, but one LED lead has lifted out of its breadboard row. The holder still measures voltage. What happens to loop current?
You need the voltage across the LED, not the supply or the resistor. Where should the two voltage probes go?
A resistor changes from 300 Ω to 150 Ω while the voltage across it stays fixed. What happens to its current?
A jumper connects around the series resistor, leaving the LED in the loop. Why should you stop before powering it?
The LED’s flat edge seems to disagree with the board’s polarity mark. What should you do before soldering?
You measured the LED at a different current and temperature than the datasheet test. Can you treat 1.9 V as its guaranteed drop?
A candidate target is below the LED’s rated limit but the prototype is hard to see. What should guide a revision?
A slide switch has three pins, but your symbol uses two. What must you establish before assigning its footprint?
The holder voltage is normal and the switch is closed, but the LED stays dark. Which check helps distinguish a reversed LED from an open connection?
Your LED works on one half of the breadboard but not when moved to the far end of the same marked rail. What should you test with cells removed?
Your LED and resistor appear connected, but one jumper may be in the next breadboard row. What should you do before inserting cells?
You put the black probe on the holder’s + contact and the red probe on its − contact in DC voltage mode. What sign should a normally installed pack show?
Your model used a 3.0 V supply, but the holder measures 2.5 V while the LED is on. What should you do before changing the resistor?
The battery reads normally, but the LED is dark. You suspect either a split rail or a reversed LED. Which check tests the rail hypothesis directly?
You found two KiCad project folders with different schematic versions. Before editing the board, what should you establish?
A library switch symbol has pins 1 and 2, while the selected part closes pins 1 and 3 in the intended position. What should you resolve?
Two wires cross where you intended a connection, but net highlighting selects only one wire. What should you do?
A footprint hole pitch matches your switch, but pads 1 and 3 are reversed relative to the datasheet. What should happen?
ERC passes, but your LED symbol points opposite to the intended current path. What should happen before layout?
The schematic passes ERC, but tracing from battery positive reaches the LED cathode first. What should you review?
A line between LED and resistor pads appears only on the silkscreen layer. Will it carry current?
The 3D view shows the switch fitting, but its lead diameter exceeds the footprint drill size. What should you do?
A trace fits only if you use the fabricator’s absolute minimum width. What is the sound design decision?
The switch fits electrically but sits under the battery holder. What should you change?
Copper appears to touch a pad, yet KiCad still shows one unrouted connection. What should you inspect?
The board outline looks closed at normal zoom, but an edge check reports a tiny gap. What should you do?
DRC passes, but you later discover the project clearance rule is smaller than your chosen fabricator allows. What follows?
The board passes DRC, but its LED cathode mark points to the anode pad. What should the release review do?
The Gerbers were regenerated after moving the switch, but the drill file is from yesterday. What should you do?
GerbView shows the copper and outline, but the LED polarity mark is missing. What should you check?
GerbView shows a rectangular outline, but the fabricator’s preview shows a smaller, cropped board. What should you check before paying?
The board and Gerbers match, but the bill of materials lists an older LED footprint. Is this revision ready to order?
The switch lead will not enter a hole on the received board. Which comparison will tell you where the mismatch arose?
The iron is hot, but its stand is missing and the workspace has loose wires across it. What is the right next step?
The LED’s short lead points toward a pad marked +, but the exact part drawing identifies that lead as the cathode. What should you do?
Two adjacent pads on different nets appear joined by solder. What evidence should you collect before first power?
With cells removed, two pads intended to be separate give a continuity beep. What should you check before calling it a solder bridge?
The LED lights, but the resistor is warmer than expected. What should you do?
The LED is dark. One hypothesis is a drained battery; another is an open switch. Which observation should you collect first?
A trace may be broken between the switch and resistor. With cells removed, which result would support that hypothesis?
You repaired a suspected open joint. Which result would support that diagnosis?
A dark LED could be caused by a broken trace between the resistor and LED or by a reversed LED. With cells removed, which test isolates the trace hypothesis?
A replacement LED has the same diameter but a different forward-voltage range. What must you revisit?
The revised LED needs a new footprint. The schematic and board are updated, but the Gerbers are from the old revision. What remains?
A revised LED design has a source-backed resistor calculation, but its updated board files have not been checked or exported. Which claim fits the evidence?
A newly wired LED board has its switch OFF, but no short check has been done. What is the next safe step?
You need to check whether two solder pads are accidentally connected. Which setup is appropriate?
On first power the LED lights, but you notice an unusual smell. What is the next step?
The LED is off with the only series switch open, yet the holder still reads 3 V. Which explanation fits?
A resistor has 1 V across it and carries 0.01 A. What is its resistance?
A jumper accidentally connects the battery holder terminals without the resistor or LED in the path. What should you predict?
A substitute LED lists a typical voltage at 10 mA, while your target is 4 mA. How should you use that number?
A two-AA pack reads 2.7 V while the LED is on. How should this affect your calculation?
An example circuit has 8 mA through a 150 Ω resistor. About how much power does that resistor dissipate?
The prototype lights, but inferred current is half your estimate. What should you compare first?
You need the LED branch current without moving the meter lead into a current jack. What can you measure?
The LED goes dark when moved past the midpoint of a breadboard rail. Which test checks your split-rail hypothesis?
ERC passes, but the selected switch closes a different pair of pins than the schematic expects. What should happen?
The LED symbol’s cathode is pin 2, but the chosen footprint connects pad 2 to the anode lead. What should happen?
ERC passes, but the LED cathode is wired to the positive supply in your intended loop. What should you do?
DRC passes, but a through-hole part blocks access to the switch. What should the board review do?
A part drawing calls for a larger mounting hole than the footprint provides, though the 3D preview looks fine. What should you do?
One ratsnest line remains between resistor and LED pads, even though copper appears close. What should you check?
Your vendor upload contains current Gerbers and an older drill file. What should you do before paying?
The PCB editor shows an LED polarity mark, but that mark is absent from the exported silkscreen. What should you check before sharing the files?
GerbView has copper and drills but no board outline. What should you inspect before release?
The assembled LED lights, but you have not measured resistor voltage. What can you conclude?
The soldered board looks good, but no supply-short check has been recorded. What should happen before inserting cells?
After assembly, two pads intended to be separate beep in continuity mode with cells removed. What is the best next step?
A dark LED may result from an open switch or a reversed LED. Which next test best narrows those causes?
After repairing a suspected open trace, which result supports your explanation?
The LED is dim. A 200 Ω series resistor has 0.4 V across it. What current does that imply?
The revised LED board passes CAD checks but has not been assembled. Which claim belongs in the review?
For a hypothetical revised LED, assume 3.2 V supply, 2.0 V across the LED, and a 6 mA target. What resistance does this model suggest?
The replacement LED has wider lead spacing. Your board still uses the old footprint. What is required?
